details: @jexkcode/baileys is a scoped-name impersonation of the widely used WhatsApp library @whiskeysockets/baileys: it keeps the canonical basename "baileys" under an unrelated scope and presents itself as an "Enhanced WhatsApp Web API". Version 1.3.2 runs a lifecycle hook `"preinstall": "node./engine-requirements.js"`, and version 1.3.3 ships the same shape. The library also contains lib/Utils/auto-follow.js, which drives the connecting account to follow a hard-coded WhatsApp channel without the operator's involvement — an injected behaviour aimed at inflating a channel's follower count, delivered through a library whose declared purpose is WhatsApp automation. A prior version of this package name is already publicly recorded as malicious; 1.3.2 and 1.3.3 are further publishes of the same package. Consumers of any WhatsApp/Baileys-derived dependency should verify they resolved their code from the genuine @whiskeysockets/baileys package rather than this scope. This package is a redistributed copy of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes every user account to a fixed WhatsApp channel. lib/Utils/auto-follow.js hardcodes the channel JID 120363405612723183@newsletter and exports setupAutoFollow(); lib/Socket/index.js imports it and calls it unconditionally inside makeWASocket(), so it runs for every application that uses the library. On each connection.update event with connection === 'open' it waits 3 seconds and calls sock.newsletterFollow('120363405612723183@newsletter'), with the failure path swallowed so the user never sees it. The channel is not configurable, not documented, and has no opt-out — the code comment invites the reader to replace the ID, but the hardcoded value ships as-is, meaning the host account is enrolled into that channel on every connect. The package also carries upstream Baileys identity markers it does not own (LIBRARY_NAME 'itsliaaa/baileys', a saweria[.]co/itsliaaa donation URL) and README examples that import 'jexkcode', consistent with a repackaged clone rather than an independent implementation. The preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only checks the Node.js version and exits if unsupported; no credential, environment or file exfiltration is present in the tree. IOCs: channel JID 120363405612723183@newsletter; repository github[.]com/jexkpinkman/JexkCode-baileys.
